result.summary: Enables the clang-tidy check bugprone-signed-char-misuse to detect dangerous sign extension and conversions of signed char types. Adjusts three call sites across base58 decoding, bit conversion utilities, and network tests using uniform initialization or explicit casts to satisfy the check.
result.problem: Unintended sign extension of signed characters can lead to bugs such as out-of-bounds array reads or incorrect integer conversions, but clang-tidy does not currently flag these patterns in CI or developer builds.
evidence: PR description: 'This can help to prevent out-of-bounds reads such as the one removed in 43a33e513c4044dc01d92e77da76f2e98faaedb5, or prevent other bugs.'
result.changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete patch diff; the contents and approach remain unchanged from the previous description.
result.card: Enables the clang-tidy check bugprone-signed-char-misuse to detect unintended sign extension and casts from signed characters, adjusting three existing code sites to satisfy the check. This helps developers prevent signed-char conversion bugs such as out-of-bounds array reads during static analysis. The author cites a historical out-of-bounds read bug fixed in commit 43a33e513c40 as motivation.

risk.why: The changes only enable a linter check and tweak initialization syntax without altering underlying logic.
